Companion Animal Travel Desk - Animal Acceptance and Boarding Guidance

This section sets out how the Companion Animal Travel Desk supports safe, courteous, and orderly travel for companion animals. Staff must give clear guidance before departure and keep each traveler informed in calm, plain language. We treat every animal with patience and every passenger with respect, and we expect the same from the welcome team, the boarding team, and any colleague who assists at the counter. <<FACT F057>> Staff must never add their own estimate, promise, or correction to that matter.

Before acceptance, the desk will confirm that the carrier, leash, harness, and other approved control items are ready for inspection, and that the passenger understands the handling steps. Any sign of distress, poor containment, or unsafe presentation must be raised at once to the senior coordinator. The desk does not admit an animal whose condition suggests immediate risk to the animal, to staff, or to other travelers, and any concern must be handled with steady judgment and without public discussion. If a traveler such as Mateo Kowalski, Anika Adeyemi, or another passenger presents supporting papers, those papers must be checked carefully and kept with the travel record in the approved file.

During boarding, staff should guide the passenger to remain attentive and should use a warm, even tone throughout. The animal must stay under control at all times, and the passenger must follow the instructions given by the welcome team. Any exception, delay, or change in arrangement must be reported through the normal desk channel before the traveler is sent onward. Where needed, the shift coordinator will arrange further review, and the passenger will be told only what is necessary for the journey. If there is any doubt, contact the duty supervisor or the Companion Animal Travel Desk immediately.
